decisions.basis: Pair 0010 dossier: NL3 clause, exact binding of the system root, HumanDriving, Power_On, and the two transition facts.
decisions.reason: The clause says that on power on the system turns into HumanDriving. The supplied facts show only a root initial edge to HumanDriving and a separate Power_On transition from HumanDriving to Autonomous; no system-owned initial edge is triggered by Power_On. The weaker reading that startup merely enters HumanDriving is excluded by the explicit Power_On condition and does not satisfy the stated obligation.
decisions.violated_obligation: On Power_On, the system owner must initially enter HumanDriving.

decisions.basis: Pair 0010 dossier: NL4.2 clause, exact bindings for Autonomous, AutonomousActive, HumanDriving, Auto Final scope, both events, and both transitions.
decisions.reason: The clause requires a transition from autonomous state to HumanDriving in auto final scope for the stated steering and brake conditions. The exact inventory places both transitions from AutonomousActive, while Autonomous is a distinct bound state and no explicit equivalence between the two scopes is supplied. Thus the required endpoint reading is established, but an alternative scope reading treating AutonomousActive as the intended autonomous state remains compatible with the supplied transition facts.
decisions.strongest_defeater: AutonomousActive may be the intended shorthand or operational scope for the autonomous state, making its transitions to HumanDriving an indirect representation of the requirement.
decisions.violated_obligation: Autonomous must transition to HumanDriving in the specified auto final scope under Human_Steering_Cmd and Brake_Pressed.

decisions.basis: Pair 0010 dossier: NL5 power-off clause, exact S2 binding, complete transition inventory, and completed backend receipt.
decisions.reason: The clause requires Autonomous to transition to AutonomousFinal on Power_Off. A terminal-state interpretation remains compatible because the supplied clause names a final state but does not itself specify whether a formal terminal edge or another completion convention is required.
decisions.strongest_defeater: AutonomousFinal may intentionally be a terminal leaf, so zero outgoing transitions may represent completion rather than a failure of termination.
decisions.violated_obligation: Autonomous mode must reach AutonomousFinal with stable completion semantics under Power_Off.

decisions.basis: Pair 0010 dossier: NL5 termination clause, exact source/model bindings, reachability and dead-end facts, and the completed V4 receipt.
decisions.reason: The clause requires autonomous mode to terminate by reaching the final state. The exact target AutonomousFinal is reachable but has no outgoing transition, and the supplied finite verification facts identify it as a reachable non-final dead end for progress purposes. The possible intentional-terminal reading is defeated here by the explicit supplied termination/completion requirement and the absence of any exact formal terminal edge or terminal fact supporting that alternative.
decisions.violated_obligation: Autonomous mode must reach AutonomousFinal and complete with stable termination.

decisions.basis: Pair 0010 dossier: NL2 containment clause and the unresolved source/model scope facts, with no exact model-element binding.
decisions.reason: The clause requires Autonomous to be a submachine state owning its stated substates. With no reproducible model-element binding or complete owned-child inventory, the required containment relation cannot be decided.
decisions.violated_obligation: Autonomous must be represented as a submachine state and must own its stated substates.

decisions.violated_obligation: Autonomous must be a composite submachine state containing the substates assigned to it.

issues.basis: The source inventory identifies the initial edge as @initial:__root__ -> HumanDriving (tr_0001), while the closed model has Power_On on HumanDriving -> Autonomous (transition:line:14). The owner hint is system, and the model's root initial transition is not a Power_On transition.
issues.expected: On power on, the system owner must initially enter HumanDriving.
issues.observed: The only closed-model initial edge is [*] -> HumanDriving; Power_On is a later HumanDriving -> Autonomous transition.
issues.reason: The exact closed model has a root initial edge to HumanDriving, but no system-owned initial edge triggered by Power On. The supplied contract binds owner=system and target=human driving mode, so the root initial edge does not establish the required power-on owner-local entry semantics.
issues.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The root initial edge does enter HumanDriving, which could satisfy a weaker requirement that startup enters HumanDriving, but it does not establish the explicitly stated power-on trigger and system-owner semantics.
issues.title: Power-on initial entry is not modeled

issues.basis: The closed transition inventory contains transition:line:19 with source HumanDriving and target Autonomous, and its trigger is Front_Distance_10_2, corresponding to the source event Front Distance > 10. The endpoint contract is therefore satisfied.
issues.expected: HumanDriving must have a transition to Autonomous for the stated front-distance condition.
issues.observed: transition:line:19 is HumanDriving -> Autonomous with trigger Front_Distance_10_2.
issues.reason: No exact HumanDriving-to-Autonomous transition is triggered by the required front-distance-greater-than-10 condition in the closed model? The closed model does contain HumanDriving -> Autonomous with Front_Distance_10_2, but the contract's endpoint relation is satisfied by that exact transition. Its trigger qualification is a separate semantic property and is not emitted here because the atomic contract property is transition_endpoints.
issues.requirement_quote: when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The exact endpoint and corresponding event are present in the closed inventory, so there is no endpoint defect.
issues.title: Human-to-autonomous endpoint comparison

issues.basis: The source inventory contains AutonomousActive -> HumanDriving transitions tr_0005 and tr_0006, while no transition has source Autonomous and target HumanDriving. The closed transition inventory likewise contains transition:line:17 and transition:line:18 from AutonomousActive, not Autonomous.
issues.expected: Autonomous must transition to HumanDriving in the specified auto final scope under the stated human steering and brake conditions.
issues.observed: Only AutonomousActive -> HumanDriving transitions exist for Human_Steering_Cmd and Brake_Pressed; no Autonomous -> HumanDriving transition exists.
issues.reason: The exact autonomous-state-to-human-driving endpoint is not present. Instead, the closed model places Human_Steering_Cmd and Brake_Pressed transitions on AutonomousActive, and the source inventory identifies Auto Final State as a distinct state. The required local-exit relation from autonomous state in auto final scope therefore has no matching transition.
issues.requirement_quote: transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: If autonomous state is intended as a shorthand for AutonomousActive, the endpoint could be viewed as represented indirectly, but the supplied source inventory distinguishes Autonomous from AutonomousActive and provides no explicit equivalence.
issues.title: Autonomous local exit has the wrong source scope

issues.basis: The source inventory contains tr_0008 HumanDriving -> AutonomousFinal on Power Off and no Autonomous -> AutonomousFinal transition. The closed inventory contains the same endpoint at transition:line:20 and no required Autonomous source edge.
issues.expected: Autonomous must transition to AutonomousFinal when Power Off occurs.
issues.observed: Power_Off is modeled only on HumanDriving -> AutonomousFinal; no Autonomous -> AutonomousFinal edge exists.
issues.reason: The required Autonomous-to-final-state endpoint is absent from the complete closed transition inventory. The only Power_Off transition is HumanDriving -> AutonomousFinal, so the autonomous completion edge is missing.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: A final-state transition exists for Power_Off, but it originates at HumanDriving, not at the required Autonomous source.
issues.title: Power-off completion edge is missing from autonomous state

issues.basis: The termination contract names Autonomous and final state. The closed model maps final state to state:AutonomousFinal:line:12; reachability facts show it is reachable; inspection and verify facts report zero outgoing transitions for that leaf.
issues.expected: The autonomous mode must terminate by reaching final state under the power-off completion behavior.
issues.observed: AutonomousFinal is reachable but has no outgoing transition; the supplied finite verification row marks deadlock:state:AutonomousFinal:line:12 refuted with outgoing_count=0.
issues.reason: The termination obligation is not closed by the endpoint fact alone. The designated AutonomousFinal target is reachable but has no outgoing transition, and the supplied verification facts explicitly report a reachable leaf without outgoing behavior. This prevents stable completion semantics for the autonomous mode from being established by the supplied closed model.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: A leaf final state may be intentional terminal semantics, so the no-outgoing fact alone does not prove that the termination contract is violated unless the contract requires a formal completion edge or stable completion interpretation.
issues.title: Autonomous termination is not demonstrably stable

issues.basis: The NL5 termination contract requires autonomous mode to terminate by reaching final state. The closed model binds AutonomousFinal to state:AutonomousFinal:line:12, and inspection-equivalent plus finite verification facts report LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and a refuted deadlock check with outgoing_count 0.
issues.expected: Autonomous mode reaches final state and completes with stable termination.
issues.observed: AutonomousFinal is reachable but has no outgoing FCSTM transition; the finite verification deadlock check for that state is refuted.
issues.reason: The required termination property is stronger than endpoint existence. The exact target AutonomousFinal is reachable, but the supplied deterministic facts show it has no outgoing transition and is therefore a reachable dead-end rather than a demonstrated stable completion of the autonomous mode. This is a termination issue on the termination contract, not a replacement of the separately satisfied endpoint contract.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source may intend AutonomousFinal to be a terminal state, in which case no outgoing transition could be intentional; however, the supplied termination contract requires completion by reaching final state, and the available deterministic facts do not establish stable completion semantics beyond the leaf condition.
issues.title: Autonomous termination is not stably completed
